==English==
{{wp|,+ting}}

===Etymology===
{{ety|en|:inh|enm:spot<ety:inh<ang:splott>>|:influence<conj:and>|dum:spotte|enm:splot}}
From {{inh|en|enm|spot}}, {{m|enm|spotte}}, partially from {{der|en|dum|spotte|t=spot, speck}}, and partially merging with {{inh|en|enm|splot}}, from {{inh|en|ang|splott|t=spot, plot of land}}, from {{inh|en|gmw-pro|*splott}}, from {{inh|en|gem-pro|*spluttaz||segment}}, from {{der|en|ine-pro|*splt-no-||an off-split, segment}}, from {{der|en|ine-pro|*(s)pel-||to split}}. 

Cognate with {{cog|frr|spot|t=speck, piece of ground}}, {{cog|nds|spot|t=speck}}, {{cog|non|spotti|t=small piece}}. See also {{m|en|splot}}, {{m|en|splotch}}.

===Pronunciation===
* {{IPA|en|/spɒt/|a=UK}}
* {{rhymes|en|ɒt|s=1}}
* {{IPA|en|/spɑt/|a=US}}
* {{audio|en|en-us-spot.ogg|a=US}}

===Noun===
{{wikidata lexeme|L5806}}
{{en-noun}}

# A [[round]] or [[irregular]] [[patch]] on the [[surface]] of a thing having a different [[color]], [[texture]] etc. and generally round in shape.
#: {{ux|en|The leopard is noted for the '''spots''' of color in its fur.}}
#: {{ux|en|Why do ladybugs have '''spots'''?}}
# A [[stain]] or [[disfigure|disfiguring]] [[mark]].
#: {{ux|en|I have tried everything, and I can’t get this '''spot''' out.}}
# A [[pimple]], [[papule]] or [[pustule]].
#: {{ux|en|That morning, I saw that a '''spot''' had come up on my chin.}}
#: {{ux|en|I think she's got chicken pox; she's covered in '''spots'''.}}
# A symbol on a [[playing card]], [[domino]], [[die]], etc. indicating its value; a [[pip]].
# {{senseid|en|modicum}} A small, unspecified [[amount]] or [[quantity]].
#: {{syn|en|Thesaurus:modicum}}
#: {{ux|en|Do come 'round on Sunday for a '''spot''' of tea, won't you?}}
# {{lb|en|slang|US}} A bill of five-dollar or ten-dollar denomination in dollars.
#: {{ux|en|Here's the twenty bucks I owe you, a ten '''spot''' and two five '''spots'''.}}
# A [[location]] or [[area]].
#: {{ux|en|I like to eat lunch in a pleasant '''spot''' outside.}}
#: {{ux|en|For our anniversary we went back to the same '''spot''' where we first met.}}
#* {{RQ:Milton Paradise Lost|book=3|passage=That '''spot''' to which I point is Paradise.|year=1873}}
#* {{quote-book|en|year=1800|author=w:William Wordsworth|title=[[s:Lyrical Ballads (1800)/Volume 2/Hart-leap Well|Hart-leap Well]]
|passage="A jolly place," said he, "in times of old! / But something ails it now: the '''spot''' is curs'd."}}
#* {{quote-web|en|year=2011|author=Tom Fordyce|title=Rugby World Cup 2011: England 12-19 France|site=news.bbc.co.uk|url=http://news.bbc.co.uk/sport1/hi/rugby_union/15210221.stm
|passage=Yachvilli made it 6-0 with a second sweet strike from 45 metres after Matt Stevens was penalised for collapsing a scrum, and then slid another penalty just wide from the same '''spot'''.}}
# A [[parking space]].
# {{lb|en|sports}} An official determination of placement.
#: {{ux|en|The fans were very unhappy with the referee's '''spot''' of the ball.}}
# A [[bright]] [[lamp]]; a [[spotlight]].
# {{lb|en|US|advertising}} A [[brief]] [[advertisement]] or [[program]] [[segment]] on [[television]].
#: {{ux|en|Did you see the '''spot''' on the news about the shoelace factory?}}
# A difficult situation.
#: {{syn|en|predicament|Thesaurus:difficult situation}}
#: {{ux|en|She was in a real '''spot''' when she ran into her separated husband while on a date.}}
# {{lb|en|gymnastics|dance|weightlifting}} One who spots ([[support]]s or [[assist]]s a [[maneuver]], or is prepared to [[assist]] if safety [[dictate]]s); a [[spotter]].
# {{lb|en|soccer}} [[penalty spot|Penalty spot]].
#* {{quote-journal|en|date=January 8, 2011|author=Chris Bevan|title=Arsenal 1 - 1 Leeds|work=BBC|url=http://news.bbc.co.uk/sport2/hi/football/fa_cup/9341711.stm|passage=
The Gunners dominated for long periods but, against the run of play, Denilson fouled Max Gradel and Robert Snodgrass put Leeds ahead from the '''spot'''.|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20260823102940/http://news.bbc.co.uk/sport2/hi/football/fa_cup/9341711.stm|archivedate=23 August 2026}}
# The act of spotting or noticing something.
#: {{ux|en|You've misspelled "terrapin" here. —Whoops. Good '''spot'''.}}
# A variety of the common domestic [[pigeon]], so called from a spot on its head just above the beak.
# A [[food fish]] ({{taxlink|Leiostomus xanthurus|species}}) of the Atlantic coast of the [[United States]], with a black spot behind the shoulders and fifteen oblique dark bars on the sides.
# The {{vern|southern redfish}}, or {{vern|red horse|novern=1}} ({{taxlink|Sciaenops ocellatus|species}}), which has a spot on each side at the base of the tail.
# {{lb|en|in the plural|brokers' slang|dated}} Commodities, such as merchandise and cotton, sold for immediate delivery.
# {{lb|en|physics}} An [[autosoliton]].
# {{lb|en|finance}} A [[decimal point]]; [[point]].
#: {{uxi|en|Twelve '''spot''' two five pounds sterling.|t=£12.25}}
# Any of various points marked on the table, from which balls are played, in [[snooker]], [[pool]], [[billiards]], etc.
# Any of the [[ball]]s marked with spots in the game of [[pool]], which one player aims to [[pot]], the other player taking the [[stripe]]s.
# {{lb|en|AU|NZ}} An [[alcoholic]] [[drink]].
#* {{quote-book|en|year=1942|author={{w|Leonard Mann (writer)|Leonard Mann}}|title=The Go-Getter|page=188
|passage=‘It's a time since I saw you, Chris. What about a '''spot'''?’}}
#* {{quote-book|en|1963|{{w|Ronald Hugh Morrieson}}|The Scarecrow||publisher=Text Classics|year_published=2012|41|To be lured into his shop for a convivial '''spot''' was disastrous.}}

===Verb===
{{wikidata lexeme|L324}}
{{en-verb}}

# {{lb|en|transitive}} To [[see]], [[find]]; to [[pick out]], [[notice]], [[locate]], [[distinguish]] or [[identify]].
#: {{syn|en|catch sight of|descry|make out|Thesaurus:spot}}
#: {{ux|en|Try to '''spot''' the differences between these two pictures.}}
#* {{quote-web
|en
|date=January 18, 2022
|author=HARDCORE MINER
|title=Gold in Taiwan – A Surprisingly Rich Mining History
|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20230406112838/https://howtofindgoldnuggets.com/taiwan-gold-mining/
|work=How to Find Gold Nuggets
|section=Early Mining History, Where to Find Gold
|text=Taiwan’s gold discovery can be traced back to 1890 during construction of the railroad between Keelung and Taipei. Workers on the project '''spotted''' gold sediments on the banks of the Keelung River between Chitu and Patu.}}
# {{lb|en|US|slang|ditransitive}} To [[loan]] a small amount of [[money]] to someone.
#: {{ux|en|I’ll '''spot''' you ten dollars for lunch.}}
# {{lb|en|ambitransitive}} To [[stain]]; to [[leave]] a spot (on).
#: {{syn|en|begrime|blot|soil|Thesaurus:dirty}}
#: {{ux|en|Hard water will '''spot''' if it is left on a surface.}}
#: {{ux|en|a garment '''spotted''' with mould}}
# {{lb|en|transitive}} To [[cover]] with spots, to [[speckle]].
#: {{syn|en|asperse|bespeckle|fleck}}
#* {{quote-book|en|year=1853|author=Robert Southey|title=The Poetical Works of Robert Southey|page=6
|text=No palm-tree rose to '''spot''' the wilderness; {{nb...}}}}
#* {{quote-book|en|year=1855|author=Percy Bysshe Shelley|title=Works|page=83
|text={{...}} many ships '''spotting''' the dark blue deep / With snowy sails, fled fast as ours came nigh, {{...}} }}
#* {{quote-book|en|year=1865|author=w:Walt Whitman|title=Sequel to Drum-Taps: When Lilacs Last in the Dooryard Bloom’d and other poems|chapter=[[w:When Lilacs Last in the Dooryard Bloom'd|When Lilacs Last in the Dooryard Bloom’d]]
|passage={{...}} Amid lanes and through old woods, where lately the violets peep’d from the ground, '''spotting''' the gray debris, {{...}}}}
# To experience {{w|vaginal spotting|vaginal}} [[spotting]]; to expel blood from the vagina.
#* {{quote-book|en|year=1988|author=Anne Dickson|author2=Nikki Henriques|title=Women on Menopause: A Practical Guide to a Positive Transition|publisher=Inner Traditions / Bear & Co|isbn=9780892812370|page=39
|text="If you've got regular periods with an IUD that's fine, but if you're starting to '''spot''' or get quite a regular loss, then it should be carefully investigated." (''Last'')}}
# {{lb|en|dialectal}} To rain slightly, in scattered, infrequent drops, for example when first beginning to rain.
#* {{quote-book|en|date=2019-04-01|author=Louise Allen|title=Least Likely to Marry a Duke: A Regency Historical Romance|publisher=Harlequin|isbn=9781488047183
|text=And it is beginning to '''spot''' with rain. I must start work on a shelter.}}
#* {{quote-book|en|date=2010-05-03|author=Celia Rees|title=Pirates!|publisher=A&C Black|isbn=9781408810354|page=57
|text={{...}} thunder growled as if to confirm his prediction. Rain was beginning to '''spot''' as he kissed me in parting. I had to hurry back to the Assembly Rooms to avoid a soaking. }}
# {{lb|en|transitive}} To [[remove]], or [[attempt]] to remove, a stain.
#: {{ux|en|I '''spotted''' the carpet where the child dropped spaghetti.}}
# {{lb|en|transitive}} To [[retouch]] a photograph on film to remove minor flaws.
# {{lb|en|transitive|gymnastics|dance|weightlifting|climbing}} To [[support]] or [[assist]] a [[maneuver]], or to be prepared to [[assist]] if safety [[dictate]]s.
#: {{ux|en|I can’t do a back handspring unless somebody '''spots''' me.}}
# {{lb|en|transitive|dance}} To keep the head and eyes [[point]]ing in a single direction while [[turn]]ing.
#: {{ux|en|Most figure skaters do not '''spot''' their turns like dancers do.}}
# {{lb|en|transitive}} To stain; to blemish; to taint; to disgrace; to tarnish, as reputation.
#: {{syn|en|besmirch|blot|denigrate|Thesaurus:defame}}
#* {{RQ:Sidney Arcadia|passage=Link not me in self same chain / With the wicked-working folk, / Who their '''spotted''' thoughts do cloak.}}
#* {{RQ:Beaumont Fletcher Comedies and Tragedies|title=Philaster|act=5|scene=2|passage=If ever I shall close these eyes but once, / May I live '''spotted''' for my perjury.}}
# {{lb|en|transitive}} To cut or chip (timber) in preparation for hewing.
# {{lb|en|transitive|mostly|snooker|and|billiards}} To place (an object) at a location indicated by a spot.
#: {{ux|en|The referee had to '''spot''' the pink on the blue spot.}}
# {{lb|en|intransitive|snooker|and|billiards}} Of a ball, to be capable of being placed on its own spot.
#: {{ux|en|The black ball won't '''spot''' – the green is in the way.}}
# {{lb|en|aviation|military|transitive}} To position (an [[aircraft]]) on the [[deck]] of an [[aircraft carrier]] ready for [[launch]] by [[catapult]].
#* {{quote-book|en|year=1959|publisher=United States. Bureau of Naval Personnel|title=Aviation Boatswain's Mate 3 & 2: Navy Training Courses|page=315
|passage=The aircraft is '''spotted''' on the catapult, and the console operator turns the crank to FIRST READY, causing the exhaust valve to close.}}
#* {{quote-journal|en|year=1990|author=Mike Harvell|journal=Airman|pages=9–37
|passage=This '''spotting''' order varies from carrier to carrier to suit the flight-deck layout. Certain aircraft must be '''spotted''' in a specific location to permit servicing, loading of ammunition, starting, maintenance, and so forth.}}
# {{lb|en|railroading|transitive}} To position (a [[locomotive]] or [[car]]) at a predetermined point, e.g., for loading or unloading.
